scope: Primary-source provenance and patient-independence wording for VinBigData/VinDr-CXR. No image downloads, no private identifier access, no training.

findings.one_image_per_patient: Not established. No explicit one-image-per-patient or patient-disjoint assertion was found in the inspected public primary documentation for the 18,000-image release.
findings.source_image_ids: PhysioNet Data Description/Overview states image identifiers are encoded from DICOM Service Object Pair (SOP) Instance Unique Identifier tag (0008,0018). These are image-instance identifiers; uniqueness does not establish unique patients.
findings.removed_metadata: PhysioNet Data de-identification and the original Scientific Data paper say PHI tags including patient ID and acquisition date/time were removed, with only processing attributes retained.
findings.split_claim: The primary release describes 15,000 training scans and 3,000 test scans. The described radiologist-independence refers to separate annotation by readers, not independence of patients.
findings.roboflow_split_limit: A published Roboflow derivative repartitioning 14,998 source images is not the original 15,000/3,000 benchmark. Patient independence cannot be inferred from its source-image filenames or original benchmark partition sizes.
findings.patient_leakage_status: Unverified rather than demonstrated. Absence of explicit patient mapping/one-patient assertion is not evidence that repeated patients exist.

source_distinction.kaggle: VinBigData competition uses 14 localized radiographic findings plus No finding; 15,000 labeled training images and 3,000 competition test images.
source_distinction.physionet: VinDr-CXR publication/release describes 22 local findings and 6 global labels of suspected disease; richer annotation taxonomy than the Kaggle 14-finding task.
source_distinction.consequence: Cite Kaggle for exact 14 classes and No finding interpretation. Cite VinDr paper/PhysioNet for source collection and de-identification, without implying the Roboflow derivative contains all 28 labels or retains the original test consensus.

priority_proxy.proposed_definition: Project-defined educational image review priority based on presence of any of the 14 annotated abnormalities, with target-negative meaning none of those14 findings annotated.
caveats: The source calls these critical findings, but this phrasing does not supply an urgency outcome label or validate an urgency policy.
The primary release says radiologists were blinded to relevant clinical information.
No finding means absence of the 14listed findings in Kaggle, not proof that the patient is healthy or needs no medical attention.
False negatives/recall should be stated against the defined annotated-abnormality target, not urgent patients or missed emergencies.
priority_proxy.suggested_report_sentence: This project simulates image review prioritization using annotated radiographic abnormalities as a proxy; it does not predict clinical urgency. Patient independence across the published derivative splits could not be verified.
